title: Log cabin colourwork throw
subtitle: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw in log-cabin construction using four DK colours.
excerpt: A 100 by 120 cm lap throw using log-cabin strip construction in four rotating DK colours. Unlike a two-colour log cabin, this uses a four-colour palette that cycles A, B, C, D around each successive ring, producing a bolder and more varied surface. About 200 g of each of four DK colours.
sourceNotes: Elizabeth Zimmermann, Knitting Without Tears (1971), §Log Cabin Squares, extends the log-cabin concept to multiple colours in the same chapter. Weldon's Practical Knitter, 6th series (1890), §Striped Afghans, documents four-colour strip-construction throws.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles. Log-cabin construction uses garter throughout.

stitchCountCheckpoints.label: Centre-square check — 11 sts at row 22 (5 cm square)
First strip check — approximately 17 sts at completion

glossaryTerms.definition: A variant of log-cabin modular construction where four colours (A, B, C, D) cycle in order through successive strips, one colour per strip. As the strips build outward from the centre, each ring of four strips shows all four colours. The result is a concentric pattern where colour relationships shift with each full rotation.

content.text: on 4 mm needles, finishing at 100 cm wide by 120 cm long.

Same modular strip method as a two-colour log cabin, but each successive strip uses the next colour in the A-B-C-D sequence. After four strips (one complete rotation around the growing rectangle), all four colours have appeared once. Budget about 200 g per colour (about 440 m / 480 yards per colour) of DK. The project is ideal for stash or multi-pack yarn. Each strip uses 15 to 35 g, making the project very manageable to store and transport.

items.name: Needles

content.text: 22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles. At this gauge, the centre square is 11 stitches × 22 rows for a 5 cm × 5 cm square. The outer strips each add about 2 cm per four-row depth. Total strips to reach 100 × 120 cm: approximately 56, each of 8 rows.

items.name: PU
items.qty: pick up stitches along a garter edge at 1 per ridge

content.text: Using Yarn A, cast on 11 stitches. Long-tail tail: (4 × 11) / 10 + 15 = 19.4 cm. Measure 25 cm. Knit every row for 22 rows (5 cm × 5 cm square). Do not cast off.

Strip 1 (Yarn B): pick up 11 sts along the right edge of the centre square (1 per ridge). Knit 8 rows garter. Cast off. Strip 2 (Yarn C): pick up sts along the bottom of the centre square + bottom of strip 1. Knit 8 rows garter. Cast off. Strip 3 (Yarn D): pick up sts along the left edge of the centre square + left side of strips 1 and 2. Knit 8 rows garter. Cast off. Strip 4 (Yarn A): pick up sts along the top of the centre square + top of all previous strips. Knit 8 rows garter. Cast off.

Continue rotating clockwise, cycling through the four colours in order A, B, C, D, A, B, C, D ... until the overall dimensions reach 100 cm wide by 120 cm long. When you set this aside, note the current colour and current strip position in the rotation.

After the centre square: 11 stitches should have been active at any point. After the first four strips (one full rotation, about 20 cm): check that the block is approximately 20 cm × 20 cm before proceeding. If not, adjust the strip depth (row count) to correct.
Colour sequence losing track: one colour was repeated or skipped. Keep a tally: write the colour letter used for each strip on a sticky note and cross it off as each strip is completed.

Block not square after four strips: the strip depth (row count) was inconsistent. Use the same row count (8 rows per strip) throughout and verify the block width and height match after each complete rotation.
Weave in all ends per strip on the wrong side. The garter-stitch fabric lies flat without blocking.
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry.

From a four-colour log cabin, try a striped-within-strip version next. Each strip uses two colours alternating every two rows. This adds a secondary stripe pattern inside the concentric-ring structure.
